2. Facts, relevant for disposal of the Rule, in brief, are that one Md Barat Ali, as plaintiff, filed Other Class Suit No.54 of 1999, before the Senior Assistant Judge, Ullapara, Sirajgonj against the Government of Bangladesh, represented by the Deputy Commissioner, Sirajgonj and others, being the defendants, with a prayer for declaration of title, in respect of the schedule property. Further case of the plaintiff-petitioner is that, the plaintiff has filed the suit as Secretary of the Pangkharua Graveyard Committee. He further claimed that, 2.59 (two point fifty nine) acres of land were granted pattan/lease by Jaminder Raj Mohani Dashya and others, who have granted the same in CS khatian No. 1 of Mouza Pangkharua, PS Ullapara, District-Sirajgonj. 

 7. Learned Advocate Mr Md Abdul Hai Sarker appeared on behalf of the petitioner. Having placed the petition alongwith the Materials on record, he mainly submits that, the suit property was recorded in CS kahtain No. 1 of Mouza-Pangkharua, PS Ullapara, District-Pabna, now Sirajgonj and belonged to Jaminder Sothis Chandra and others and they had granted the suit property to the plaintiff for the purpose of using as the graveyard. In support of his contention, he has referred to a piece of paper marked as Ext. 6, whereby, according to his submission, the suit property was granted to one Showkat Ali Mondal, the then President of a committee of the aforesaid graveyard. He also submits that, in the DP khatian No. 580 (Ekhibit 4), it has been recorded that, the suit property has been shown as graveyard, represented by its President Md Barat Ali Mondal (who is the plaintiff). He next submits that, the trial court having seen the aforesaid document of grant granting the lease (Exhibit 6) as well as the DP khatian No. 580 (Exhibit 4) has rightly found that, the plaintiff is the owner and possessor of the suit property. But, the appellate court, while considering the appeal has wrongly assessed the evidence on record and upon wrong findings, it has set-aside the judgment and decree of the trial court. He also submits that, the document of the grant of pattan of lease is unregistered and unstamped. However, the PW 3 Hachen Ali has stated in his deposition that he was present at the time of granting that pattan. Therefore, he submits, the appellate court's finding that, the deed was not a correct deed of pattan was totally based on misreading of evidence and misconception of law and facts. He proceeds on that, the PWs have consistently deposed that, the suit property was never occupied by the Government and the Government had never possessed the same, but the appellate court has totally overlooked the material evidence and thereby committed error of law in its decision and as such, this Rule has merit and the same is liable to be made absolute. 

 8. Learned Deputy Attorney-General Mr Mohammad Monirul Islam, Mr Sarwar Akhter Masud, AAG and Mrs. Shama Akhtar, AAG have appeared on behalf of the opposite party. The learned DAG having placed the petition and drawing my attention to the paragraph No. 1 as well as schedule to the plaint, first of all submits that, the suit property has been described as 2.50 (two point five zero) acres of land used as graveyard. Therefore, the evidence of the PWs saying that, the suit property is more than one Bigha in the local measurement is beyond the quantity of land (2.50 sfak) as per pleadings and is admissible. He also pointed out that, the trial court did not pass any decree for 2.50 (two point five zero) acres of land. It had passed the decree for 2 (two and half staks. Even then, he also submits, the decree of the trial court is wrong, in view of the clear finding of the appellate court that, the plaintiff did not submit the RS or SA khatain to describe the suit property. Therefore, the trial court's decree, based on RS. Plot No. 1239 without any RS khatain being placed or proved before it, was totally not supported by documentary evidence, while pleadings of the plaintiff is not an evidence. Moreso, the appellate court has examined the certified copy of CS khatain No. 1, which has been marked as Exhibit 1 and found that, the CS Plot No. 1, exhibit 1, was a pond and that CS Plot comprises 2.54 acres of pond with banks, whereas the plaintiff's claim is 2.50 acres of solid land. The learned DAG further submits that, the pond or any water body cannot be granted as pattan for grave-yard. He next submits that, the appellate court has rightly appreciated that, when the nature of the entire suit property even with reference to DP khatain No. 580 (Exhibit 4) is pond (water body with banks), very surprisingly the plaintiff claimed that, he has been using the same as graveyard and possessing the same through cultivation, which is totally absurd. During cross-examination, the DAG points out that, the PW 1 has stated that, there was graveyard in the suit property, which the appellate court has rightly held that, the judgment of the trial court based on mere oral evidence of the PWs without any documentary evidence showing it nature, was totally erroneous and not tenable in the eye of law. He also submits that, the appellate court has rightly assessed the question of lease or pattan of 2.50 decimals of water body or pond to the plaintiff and the same has rightly disbelieved. As regards, the unstamped and unregistered document, purported to be a deed of lease and marked as exhibit 6, the learned law Officers proceeds on that, apparently, this exhibit-6 is a subsequent creation in as much as, the green ink used on this document shows that, the ink has been used recently. Therefore, the appellate court has rightly disbelieved the case of the plaintiff and has rightly set aside the findings of the trial court on this fact. They conclude that in passing the impugned judgment and decree, the appellate court has committed no error of law or facts. The learned DAG submits that, this property is the property of the Government, which the plaintiff has been trying to grab in connivance with the PWs or by gaining over the PWs. The plaintiff, he proceeds on, has apparently abstained from filing the relevant SA and RS khatian for concealing the actual nature and quantity of the suit propert, which is a pond or water body, except for 2½ (two and half) decimals, which has been claimed by the plaintiff, in this plaint, as graveyard granted by the Jaminder. The Jaminder granted 2.50 acres of land (indeed a Fond) for graveyard is not the case of the plaintiff. Therefore, the depositions of PWs are not supported by the pleading and their depositions are apparently false, which, they have given being gained over by the plaintiffs, they submit. He next argue that, in the DP khatain, the nature of the suit property is a pond (exhibit 4), but, the plaintiff has claimed it as a graveyard. If he is Secretary, he ought to have filed the relevant minutes before the trial court. As such he has no locus-standi to file this case. He also submits that, in no circumstances, the plaintiff has been able to prove its case before the court However, in reply to a query made from the Bench, the learned DAG submits that, if there is a graveyard, on 2½ (two and half) decimals of land, then that may be from time in memory the suit property is using as graveyard. The learned DAG concludes that, the impugned judgment and decree passed by the appellate court suffers from no illegality or from any other lacuna, whatsoever, and this Rule has no merit and the same may be discharged. 

 12. Moreso, the appellate court has examined the certified copy of CS khatain No. 1, which has been marked as Exhibit 1 and found that, the CS Plot No. 1 (exhibit 1) is a pond or water body with banks and that comprises 2.54 acres of land, whereas the plaintiff's claim is 2.50 staks of land only. It also appears that, the pond or water body cannot be granted by way of pattan for using as graveyard. Besides, the nature of the suit property even in the DP khatain No. "580 (Exhibit 4) is pond or water body. This cannot be granted by the Government for using graveyard, nor can be possessed for cultivation by the plaintiff, as stated in the plaint. 

 14. The appellate court has rightly disbelieved the question of lease or pattan of 2.50 (two and half) decimals of land to the plaintiff based on a white unstamped and unregistered deed (exhibit 6).
